title: Talking-heads attention (Shazeer et al. 2020), pre-softmax head mixing, identity-initialized, in all six Peri-LN blocks on the 115-fable hybrid ALiBi/NoPE Lean incumbent (4,800,384 params)
description: P34 x P32 follow-up (new mechanism): each block gets a learned (8, 8) matrix that mixes the eight heads' pre-softmax logit maps (content score plus that head's ALiBi recency bias) before the causal mask and softmax, identity-initialized so training starts as exactly 115. The hybrid keep says content lookup (NoPE heads) and recency (ALiBi heads) both matter; mixing lets a head attend by 'the most recent line matching this name', a conjunction no single softmax head can express, which should give a better round-1 RL start on proofs of length >= 7 where more same-name candidates compete.
hypothesis: Softmax attention in one head scores keys by a single logit; ALiBi heads score by recency, NoPE heads by content. Long proofs (>= 7 lines) have more earlier lines and more repeated name/rule tokens, so a pure content head is diluted by lookalike candidates while a pure recency head cannot pick the right one. A pre-softmax mix of head logits builds 'content AND recency' scores in the mixed heads, sharpening citation lookup exactly where longer proofs make it harder. Identity init keeps 115's solution reachable; the mixing matrices train on AdamW without decay so identity is not shrunk away.
expected_delta: -45 to +45 theorems at >=7 (central +8); the mixed-head cost is a slower unfused attention path, predicted 10-25% fewer pretraining steps (about 3,200-3,800 vs 115's 4,204-4,263) with val loss within 0.002 of 115, and RL sampling within 10% of 115's samples/s

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads as in 115, CHANGED: pre-softmax talking-heads mixing of the eight logit maps in every block (identity init)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits added to the explicit q.k logits before the head mixing; -inf causal/padding mask applied after mixing, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 113-fable: only the ALIBI_SLOPES constant (N_ALIBI = N_HEAD // 2 = 4 ALiBi heads with the standard 4-head slope set, then 4 zeros). PeriLNBlock, ALiBiGPT (bias build, key positions in caches[0], mask handling), width, heads, depth, GELU, untied embedding/readout, ln_f, init, optimizer and schedule are byte-identical to 113. The slope-0 heads see attention logits with no positional term at all, so their only position information is the causal mask (NoPE, as in 111-fable but on half the heads)
arch.n_params_detail: identical to 113-fable and 107-claude: 4,800,000 (vocab 107); slopes buffer is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py (its ALIBI_SLOPES = (1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256, 0, 0, 0, 0)), replace blocks with PeriLNBlock as in pretrain.py, then load state (same keys as 107/113). Loading these weights into 113's model (slopes 1/2..1/256) or a plain fork GPT (RoPE) gives a different function. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: unchanged from 113 (caches[0] holds key positions; slope-0 heads get a zero bias plus the -inf mask). CPU check with the pinned fork 51604b3: 2-sequence prefill of 8 tokens plus 4 cached one-token steps vs the full forward, max abs logit diff 1.0e-6; training loss/backward run; 4,800,000 params
arch.attention: talking heads (Shazeer et al. 2020), pre-softmax only: per block a learned (8, 8) head-mixing matrix applied to the logit maps (content score + per-head ALiBi bias) before the causal mask and fp32 softmax; identity init; explicit matmul attention instead of SDPA; 64 new params per block

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
optimizer.mix_group: the six (8, 8) mixing matrices: AdamW lr 1e-3 (same schedule), weight_decay 0, betas (0.9, 0.95); excluded from Muon and from the orthogonal init

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1
